title: Pectin delays gastric emptying and increases satiety in obese subjects
authors: Di Lorenzo C, Williams CM, Hajnal F, Valenzuela JE
followUp: two test days at least 48 h apart
population: Obese adults, 8 women and 1 man, mean body mass index 45.1, mean age 42.3 years, Los Angeles County-University of Southern California Medical Center
funder: not stated. The article gives affiliations and thanks two individuals for manuscript preparation; it carries no funding statement. PubMed lists no grant support.
inKindSupport: Highly purified human pancreatic polypeptide standard was a gift of Dr R. Chance.
result: Randomised double-blind crossover: 15 g pectin or 15 g methylcellulose added to a 250 kcal egg sandwich. Gastric half-emptying time 116.1 ± 23.1 min with pectin against 70.7 ± 17.3 min with methylcellulose (mean ± SEM, p < 0.001); residue at 120 min 49.6 ± 8.1% against 25.7 ± 9.5%. Satiety score 97.8 ± 6.8 against 74.4 ± 16.7 (p < 0.001); time to next meal 10.6 ± 5.1 h against 6 ± 2.5 h (p < 0.05). Postprandial cholecystokinin and pancreatic polypeptide did not differ.
